pick.mechanic_fr: Les maisons d'édition exigent dès aujourd'hui des certificats d'originalité et soumettent tout manuscrit à des tests anti‑IA, bloquant signatures et avances en attente.
pick.why: Marin's stalled novel and Romy's reporting would be directly affected by a sudden industry freeze and new verification rules.

draft.premise_fr: Margaux répète «La même chose ?». Gus dit que ton ordre te définit. Romy arrive avec sa caméra et demande si c'est toi, «l'héritage». Lila sourit: elle veut que tu choisisses ton ordre et dises pourquoi tu restes.
draft.setup_native: Margaux asks for your usual order at the bar while friends tease you. Choose the order and say why you are still in Paris.
draft.objective_native: Choose your usual order at Le Mistral and give a brief reason why you are staying (one or two short sentences).
draft.objective_semantics: The learner must (1) state a café order (drink) and (2) give a simple reason for staying in Paris now (because of family papers / to sort Odile's succession / to stay with friends). This practices giving a reason and a consequence in short present or past tenses.
draft.causal_reason: A daily ritual becomes identity: the group teases the learner into choosing an order and explaining their presence. Romy's question raises the stakes: the learner's answer will set a 'usual order' and make them publicly 'habitué'.

chapter.dramatic_question: Quelle boisson deviens-tu au Mistral, et est-ce que cela veut dire que tu restes ?
possible_developments: Le lecteur choisit une boisson et avoue qu'il reste pour les papiers de succession.
Le lecteur choisit une boisson et dit qu'il reste pour aider Margaux à garder le café.
Le lecteur choisit une boisson et dit qu'il reste pour Lila et la vie d'ici.

draft.plant_fr: Une tasse marquée «habituel» sur le plateau derrière le zinc.

panels.narration_fr: Le Mistral est plein. La pluie tambourine aux carreaux.

dialogue.text_native: Your soup waits for you afterwards.

panels.visual_direction: Wide shot: the bar at Le Mistral. Margaux dries a glass. Gus and Marin stand near the booth, laughing. Lila leans on the counter.
panels.alt_native: Wide view of the bar with people talking; a woman drying a glass at the counter.

dialogue.text_fr: Votre commande dit qui vous êtes.
dialogue.text_native: Your order says who you are.

panels.visual_direction: Close-up on Margaux at the counter, looking at the learner and holding a chalk pad.
panels.alt_native: Close-up of the bartender asking a customer their order; a man beside her smiles.

dialogue.text_fr: Allez, choisis et dis-nous pourquoi tu restes.
dialogue.text_native: Come on, choose and tell us why you are staying.

panels.visual_direction: Medium shot: Romy leans with her small camera, curious. Lila watches, amused.
panels.alt_native: A journalist leans forward with a camera; a friend nudges the customer to answer.

panels.narration_fr: On attend ta réponse. Le café retient son souffle.
panels.visual_direction: Close-up on the empty space where the learner stands (no dialogue panel). Everyone watches expectant; a plate with a cup is drawn near Margaux's hand.
panels.alt_native: Close-up of the empty space before the counter; everyone looks at the customer, waiting.

draft.suggested_response_fr: Je prends un café crème, parce que je reste pour régler les papiers d'Odile.
draft.hint_native: Say your drink (e.g., 'un café crème') and a short reason why you are staying (for example, 'parce que je reste pour régler les papiers').
draft.translation_native: Margaux asks "The same as usual?" Choose your order and briefly explain why you are staying.

season_checklist.change_before: Your order was private; you had no usual order.
season_checklist.change_after: You have a named usual order at Le Mistral and a public reason for staying.
season_checklist.turn_want: You must want to say your usual order and why you remain in Paris.
season_checklist.hook_fr: À suivre… quelqu'un écrira ton nom au tableau du zinc.
season_checklist.complication: Tomorrow, the radiator dies and someone brings soup; the cold becomes an obstacle.

refusals.hint: The narration addresses the learner as "vous" while the character speaks to them as "tu". Pick one and use it everywhere: switching between tu and vous inside a scene reads as a mistake to a learner who is being taught the difference.
